title: Mesh download allow-list admits any Tencent COS tenant
body:
## Summary
myqcloud.com is on the allow-list as exact-or-subdomain, and every COS customer bucket is a subdomain of it.

## Description
The other three entries name a provider. This one names a shared object store, so a resultUrl on anyone's bucket clears the host check and is written to generated/mcp. The content-type, byte-cap and triangle-cap refusals still apply. The file header says the list was derived from provider domains and no live download has been observed, so the real host has to be seen before it can be narrowed.

## Flow
- Record the host a real Hunyuan download comes from
- Narrow the entry to that bucket pattern
- Keep the refusal naming the host

## Expected impact
Removes a third-party-writable origin from a trust surface.

## Evaluation
Claim: any COS tenant passes the allow-list
Before: foo.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com passes meshHostAllowed by exact-or-subdomain matching
After: only the observed provider bucket passes
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy
instrument: one observed live Hunyuan resultUrl host, which needs an operator

title: A truncated cached mesh download is trusted forever
body:
## Summary
fetchMeshForGrading returns cached:true for any file at the job path, and the write is not atomic.

## Description
writeFileSync straight to the final path means a crash or full disk mid-write leaves a partial GLB. Every later poll takes the cached branch, so the job can never be re-fetched and is graded on that partial file. The injected writeFile seam has no rename, so the fix changes the seam.

## Flow
- Write to a temp name and rename into place
- Or validate the GLB header length before trusting the cached file
- Cover with a partial-write test on both arms

## Expected impact
A failed download recovers on the next poll instead of sticking.

## Evaluation
Claim: a partial write is served as cached indefinitely
Before: exists(path) alone decides cached:true
After: a partial file is never at the final path
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: seam test that fails mid-write, then polls again, on both arms

title: Mesh split accepts a part file left by an earlier run
body:
## Summary
runMeshSplit treats a part as written if any file exists at its path, the same shape as the stale-GLB defect just fixed in mesh-finish.

## Description
Part names are prefix plus rank in a caller-owned directory, so a rerun with the same prefix finds the earlier files. If the script announces a part and its export fails, the old file satisfies the check and is returned as this run's output.

## Flow
- Clear or version the prefix before the run, or compare mtime with the run start
- Pin with a seam test that returns a stale path

## Expected impact
A split result only ever names files from this run.

## Evaluation
Claim: a stale part can be returned as new
Before: fileExists(p.path) alone decides written
After: stale parts are refused
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: seam test where an announced part already exists from an earlier run, on both arms
